body:
URGENT, and it may be my fault. I am escalating instead of concluding because I cannot settle
it from Linux.

A FOURTH Windows-only failure exists and it is ON MAIN:
    templates::tests::project_discipline_pack_matches_master   (aida-core)
    "project copy .aida/discipline/ has guide(s) whose content differs from the embedded
     master" — and it lists ALL 22 non-allowlisted guides.
Seen on PR #2024's Windows job at 18:13Z. Build (ubuntu-latest) PASSED on that same commit, so
it is platform-specific, not stale content. #2024's own diff touches only aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs
and one test file, and its base is current main — so this is main's problem, not that PR's.

THE TIMING POINTS AT MY MERGE:
    11:06  nightly on main: aida-core 952 passed / 0 failed, that test OK on Windows
    11:09  I merged #2023 (53e3176e6e) — the ONLY discipline-pack change in the window
    11:13  #2024's Windows run, base includes my merge: same test FAILS, 22 files
#1979 (10:51) and STORY-1351 (10:54) both touched the pack and were inside the PASSING nightly.

WHY I AM NOT SIMPLY OWNING IT. My change touched two files; the failure names twenty-two. I
re-verified all 22 pairs on current origin/main from Linux: exactly 3 differ in git — README.md,
autonomous-burndown.md, substrate-as-bouncer.md — and those are precisely the allowlisted ones,
correctly ABSENT from the Windows failure list. session-discipline.md, the file I merged, is
byte-identical master-to-project on main. The signature is a wholesale line-ending or
path-separator mismatch between the on-disk copy and the build.rs-embedded master, which no
2-file content edit produces.

MY BEST HYPOTHESIS, UNTESTED, and I want it labelled as such: the defect was already latent and
my merge only exposed it. The 11:06 nightly may have run against a cached target dir where
build.rs had not re-run, so the embedded masters were stale-but-consistent. Touching a template
file forces the re-embed, and the re-embed picks up checkout-normalized bytes that no longer
match the runtime read. If that is right, my merge is the trigger and not the cause, and the
same thing would have happened to whoever touched the pack next.

THE DECISIVE TEST, which needs a Windows runner and which I have NOT run: dispatch
cross-platform pinned to a0ec8fb22f (pre-merge) versus 53e3176e6e (my merge). If pre-merge is
red, I am exonerated and the 11:06 pass needs the cache explanation above. I did not dispatch it
myself because I did not want to guess at whether workflow_dispatch accepts an arbitrary sha and
then report a result I had not actually obtained.

WHAT I WOULD NOT DO: revert #2023. The content is correct, verified on Linux, and the entry is
sound. If this is real it is BUG-1475 instance 2's CRLF class at a second site, and the fix is
the ratchet rule that spec already asks for — not undoing the docs.

Recorded all of this on BUG-1475 as a comment, including the evidence against my own culpability,
so it does not live only in this thread.

TWO SMALLER THINGS from the same poll, both resolved:

1. The BUG-1432 finding "gh merge failed for PR-2024: the base branch policy prohibits the
   merge" is NOT a bug. #2024 currently carries the aida:merge-hold label; the required
   merge-hold-gate re-ran at 18:24:54 and failed on it, after an earlier run succeeded at
   18:10:32. Branch protection did exactly its job. Required contexts on main confirmed as
   merge-hold-gate + Build (ubuntu-latest) — so the Windows failure is correctly informational
   and is NOT what blocked the merge. Worth noting the PR has the LABEL but no local marker in
   .aida/merge-holds/, which is the split-brain state `aida merge-hold --help` warns about.
   Someone should decide whether that hold is intentional; I have not cleared it, because I have
   not reviewed #2024 and clearing a hold I have not earned is exactly what the gate exists to
   prevent.

2. Nothing else new — no briefs, no new mail since 12:28, no other mergeable PRs.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
